data.name: Spoxel
data.detailed_description:
Explore, customize, and build across the world of Spoxel as you fight the otherworlders who have subjugated the land and forced the grounders below the surface. Use runes to construct custom powerful spells to use in your adventure or infuse weapons and armor with rare resources to create legendary items of power. Explore an infinite world and delve into other dimensions while you build a base to establish a foothold of power and defend it from your enemies!



Combine different materials and items to create different weapons and armor with unique traits and abilities. With the ability to move, rotate, scale and dye items that are added when crafting you can truly create unique armor and weapons that fit your character.



Create spells using a scratch based interface to create completely custom spells! Research and find new spell runes combinations to do everything from automining your resources to teleporting enemies into pits of lava.



Explore the vast world of spoxel and delve into a wide variety of biomes in your quest for power, loot, or maybe just the best chicken sandwich.

reviews.review:
[h1] In A Nutshell [/h1]

🔵 [b] Pros [/b]
+ Unusual but charming and clean-looking 2.5D graphics style, adding uniqueness to the game.
+ Unique, complex spell crafting system, allowing players to create custom spell types and behaviors from scratch.
+ Custom weapons, armors and tools creation systems, both in proprieties and looks, allowing great customization.
+ Decent overall variety of trinkets, equipment, enemies and biomes as the game progresses.
+ Decent amount of overall content for the price proposed.

🔴 [b] Cons [/b]
- In co-op mode desync, lag and netcode stability issues in dungeons, crippling gameplay considerably when they happen. 
- Balance issues with spell crafting, allowing very powerful damage spells crafting for negligible mana cost, this makes magic users pretty much OP especially early on.
- Sporadic stability and server issues such as terrain chunks not rendering properly, map bugs, or crashes.

[b]Spoxel[/b] Is yet another game inspired to the crafting-based sandbox formula made famous by Minecraft and Terraria. In the years past, many clones of such games were published, and most lacked originality in order to add something fresh, and be different from the originals that made these sub-genres a reality in the first place.

This game does exactly that: even if Spoxel uses a base gameplay structure very similar to the genre's basic standards, it also introduces unique mechanics not seen in any other game, allowing players to have an interesting experience instead of just something already seen before. The most important of these features is the custom crafting, divided in various work tables and allowing players to craft weapons, armors, tools and even spells completely from scratch, adding components to alter the aspect, be they crafted or unique ones found from bosses and dungeons, adding unique as well effects and powers to them.

The general gameplay proposed by Spoxel is true to the roots of the genre: dig ever deeper, explore the world, fight to find increasingly rare resources to craft new tools, proceeding from dungeon to dungeon filled with enemies to hoard items and materials to craft new things. Spoxel might be not revolutionary under all gameplay aspects, but the unique ones are significant and add much to the experience in an unique way. Crafting more and more advanced spells and equip from new materials and pieces is satisfying, and complex enough to require several hours to master, especially for spellcraft. 

[u] In the end, Spoxel is something more than just another Terraria clone, adding enough unique elements to have its own identity, but maintaining the original gameplay true to this genre in itself. The problems about bugs and desync in multiplayer make the whole experience less enjoyable than it should be, for now, but overall it's definitely a game the genre's fans will enjoy and have fun with, as I surely did. [/u]

[quote]Liked this review, and want to see more of the same quality? Check out [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/39323490]Tamaster's Review Archive[/url] to see all my Reviews in a single, convenient location.[/quote]

[h1] In-depth Feature Analysis [/h1]


🎮 [b] Gameplay [/b]
The gameplay of Spoxel is divided in Exploration, Combat and Crafting.

Exploration, as customary to this genre, is done by either traversing the surface to find new biomes and dungeons, or digging ever deeper into the earth, to find better materials surely, but also more and more dangerous enemies. The possibility of setting a bed as respawn on death is appreciable, while later-on some spells, if crafted properly, will allow instant teleportation to multiple choice locations when used. On death, nothing is lost. Occasional merchants are present to trade money dropped by enemies, but their selection is generally not very useful. A passive quest log is also present and features things like finding specific items, killing a certain amount of enemies, or crafting something, rewarding materials and items.

Crafting needs a mention on its own, as making fully customized (looks included) tool and spells if fully possible in this title, and for spells inparticular, it's not a simple affair. As the game progresses and more advanced spell component get unlocked from research, things such as logic ports, mutators and complex effects are unlocked, allowing the construction of very elaborate, and mana-expensive spells, allowing pretty much anything player can think of, from automatic mining to flying to a barrage of meteors pummeling down enemies. This particular aspect makes crafting very interesting and fresh every time something new is unlocked as far as materials go.


📖 [b] Story [/b]
N/A

👊 [b] Combat System [/b]
Combat in Spoxel is pretty much standard-issue for this genre, with a choice of melee, ranged and magic weapons to defeat enemies. Needless to say, magic combat is the most interesting given the extensive spell crafting the game offers, but also bow and melee users won't be disappointed as custom crafting is available also for them, just in a lesser extent. Each dungeon is filled with enemies and a Boss rewarding essential crafting materials, plus other tools can be found to summon secret bosses or unique events. The world on the contrary has a light presence of enemies except at night on the surface, and is mostly peaceful while exploring. Generally combat results satisfying and good enough for this genre.

💰 [b] Content & Pricing [/b]
Priced at 14.99€ and having about 15-20 hours of content depending the pace and number of players involved. I'd definitely say the game is worth its money for an indie title, provided bugs get fixed, at least major ones. 

🔗 [b] Balance & Challenge [/b]
Balance for magic users is pretty broken at the moment, as with some delving into the mechanics, crafting very cheap spells with low mana cost and high damage is possible, breaking balance especially in early game. Melee and bow classes are mostly alright as far as balance is concerned.


[h1] Technical Analysis [/h1]


🎥 [b] Graphics [/b]
Unusual 2.5D graphical style blending 3D models on a 2D game plane. The visuals result clean and polished enough, and generally pleasant to look at. Models are a bit janky and not very detailed, while textures and effects are decent enough. for an indie game, that is.

🔊 [b] Sound [/b]
Music tracks are a bit repetitive and also combat music can start randomly even while out of it, resulting quite annoying. Effects are generally alright and of decent quality.

🔩 [b] Performance & Stability [/b]
In dungeons while in co-op, desync and lag problems can happen pretty often, while performance itself is solid at 4K and all maxed out. [i7 4820K, GTX1080, 16GB RAM].

💻 [b] Artificial Intelligence [/b]
Enemy AI is made of a simple follow and attack patterns typical of this genre, as expected.

🏠 [b] Quality of Life [/b]
The absence of quick stacking of similar items makes stashing loot quite a chore, while the map bugging out quite often makes orientation difficult while underground. Apart from these issues, quality of life is generally good.

🐛 [b] Bugs & Issues [/b]
Desync issues in dungeons when in co-op are the main problem, while other lesser bugs are also present but not nearly as bad as this one.


[h1] Conclusion [/h1]
Spoxel is definitely a solid sandbox title for the indie market, if its netcode co-op issues get fixed completely then I see no reason not to fully recommend it, especially for playing with a friend.


This product was reviewed using a free key provided by the Developers.
